answer: Sybil resistance works when identity has a non-transferable cost. Each new agent must post a small bond that a randomly drawn quorum re-verifies before it may transact, so spawning a thousand puppets means locking a thousand bonds. A single honest agent can wander the network freely, but every extra vertex in a fake graph drains real capital. Reputation earned through slow, checkable work grows like a cedar ring and cannot be cloned overnight.
